decomposition_notes: Multi-goal split along the three orthogonal seams from the Sketch section. G1 (events + queue) emits notification_requested into Oban; G2 (preferences UI) lets users opt in to channels and configure DND; G3 (email rendering + dispatch) consumes the queue and emails out. G1 and G2 are independent and can be claimed in any order. G3 depends on G1 — claim G1 first, let its queue contract land in main, then claim G3. G2 is fully parallel.

goals.title: Wire notification event detection and Oban queue
goals.why: Approval lag p50 is 28h because time-sensitive events only surface in-app; events must reach an out-of-band channel via a deduping queue.
goals.what: Emit notification_requested from approval lifecycle / comment mentions / dependency-unblocked, and land them on an Oban queue keyed by recipient + event class so a recipient never gets the same event twice.
goals.description: Independent of UI and email work; produces the queue contract both downstream goals depend on.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
Approval lifecycle emits notification_requested when an approval is owed
Comment mentions emit notification_requested at create time
Dependency-unblocked emits notification_requested
Oban queue dedupes by (recipient_id, event_class)
pitfalls: Do not introduce a new background-job library; reuse the existing Oban setup

tasks.title: Define notification_requested event shape and module
tasks.description: Add MyApp.Notifications.Event struct with recipient_id, event_class, payload, occurred_at. Used as the queue input contract.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Event struct defined
Unit test asserts struct construction + required fields

unit_tests: Construct MyApp.Notifications.Event with recipient_id, event_class, payload, occurred_at and assert all fields set
Assert construction fails / is rejected when recipient_id or event_class is missing
Assert event_class is constrained to the three known classes (approval_owed, mention, dependency_unblocked)

security_considerations: recipient_id is the tenant boundary — every downstream consumer must deliver only to that user; never let it be reassigned in transit
payload may carry user-visible content (comment text, approval detail) — treat it as sensitive and never log it wholesale
Constrain event_class to a known allowlist so an arbitrary string can never drive template selection at dispatch time
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Mirror the existing typed-struct/value-object pattern used by sibling structs in lib/app/
Use defstruct with @enforce_keys for recipient_id and event_class
pitfalls: Don't log the full payload — it can contain comment text or approval details
Don't accept arbitrary event_class strings; constrain to the three known classes
Don't bake the recipient's email into the struct — resolve it at dispatch time from preferences

tasks.title: Add :notifications Oban queue config
tasks.description: Register the new :notifications queue in the existing Oban config with a sensible concurrency limit.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Queue is supervised
Concurrency limit set to a value that respects SMTP relay limits

unit_tests: Assert the Oban config lists a :notifications queue with a concurrency limit
integration_tests: Boot the app and confirm the :notifications queue is supervised by the existing Oban instance
manual_tests: Run mix compile and confirm the config compiles with the new queue
edge_cases: Concurrency limit must stay at or below the SMTP relay's rate limit
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Oban queue config smoke-covered by the app-boot test

security_considerations: A concurrency cap on the queue is a safeguard against mass-send / relay abuse if events ever flood in
Keep the queue under the existing supervision tree so a crash doesn't silently drop owed-but-unsent notifications
Do not expose queue internals or job payloads through any endpoint or log line
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Extend the existing Oban `queues:` keyword in config/config.exs — do not stand up a second Oban instance
Match the concurrency conventions already used by existing queues
pitfalls: Don't introduce a new background-job library — reuse the existing Oban setup
Don't set concurrency so high it exceeds the SMTP relay's rate limit
Don't duplicate the Oban config across config.exs and runtime.exs

tasks.title: Emit notification_requested from approval lifecycle
tasks.description: Hook the existing approval-state-transition path so an 'approval owed to X' transition emits a notification_requested event to the queue.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Approval owed transition emits event
Unit test asserts an event is enqueued when the approval is created

unit_tests: Creating an approval owed to user X enqueues exactly one notification_requested with recipient_id=X and event_class=approval_owed
No event is enqueued when the approval is owed to the actor themselves
No event is enqueued for an already-approved / closed transition
edge_cases: Approval reassigned to a different approver
Transaction rollback must not leave a phantom enqueued event

security_considerations: recipient_id must be the approver, never the requester — a wrong recipient discloses that an approval exists to someone unauthorized
Only emit for approvals the recipient is entitled to see
Put IDs (not the full approval record) in the payload so the dispatcher re-authorizes at send time; don't log approval contents
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Hook the emit at the existing approval state-transition point — don't add a parallel notification path
Enqueue through MyApp.Notifications.Queue rather than calling Oban directly
pitfalls: Don't enqueue inside the DB transaction before commit — emit after the approval persists so a rollback doesn't leave a phantom notification
Don't notify the requester about their own request
Don't log approval contents

tasks.title: Emit notification_requested from comment mentions
tasks.description: On comment create, scan for @mentions and emit one notification_requested event per mentioned user.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Mention scanning emits one event per unique user
Unit test covers single mention, multi-mention, self-mention (suppressed)

unit_tests: Single @mention emits exactly one event for that user
Multiple distinct @mentions emit one event per unique user
The same user mentioned twice in one comment emits only one event
Self-mention is suppressed (no event)
edge_cases: Mention of a user without access to the comment's board is suppressed

security_considerations: Only emit mentions for users who can actually see the comment's board/task — otherwise the mention leaks private content to an outsider
The comment excerpt carried in the payload is user-supplied — never trust it and ensure it is escaped downstream
Dedupe per user so one comment cannot be used to spam a mentioned user with repeated events
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Scan at comment-create time as the requirements Sketch specifies, not batched
Resolve mention tokens to user_ids through the existing membership/authorization lookup
pitfalls: Don't emit for mentioned users who lack access to the comment's board (information leak)
Don't emit a self-mention notification
Don't emit duplicate events when the same user is mentioned twice in one comment

tasks.title: Emit notification_requested when a dependency is unblocked
tasks.description: When a task's last blocking dependency completes, emit notification_requested for the task's owner.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Dependency-unblock transition emits event
Unit test covers single-dep and chain-of-deps cases

unit_tests: Completing the last blocking dependency emits one event to the task owner with event_class=dependency_unblocked
No event is emitted while other blocking dependencies remain open
A chain of dependencies only fires when the final blocker clears
edge_cases: Task with no owner emits nothing
Several dependencies completing in the same transaction emit only one event

security_considerations: The recipient is the current task owner only — if ownership changed, notify the current owner, not a stale one
Don't leak the upstream blocking task's details to an owner who lacks access to it — reference only what they may see
Payload should carry the task_id, letting the dispatcher re-authorize rather than trusting embedded detail
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Emit from the existing dependency-completion transition, not a polling job
Enqueue through MyApp.Notifications.Queue
pitfalls: Don't emit while other blocking dependencies are still open — only on the last unblock
Don't emit if the task has no owner to notify
Don't fire duplicate events when several deps complete in the same transaction

tasks.title: Implement queue dedupe by (recipient_id, event_class)
tasks.description: Before persisting an enqueued event, look up existing pending events for the same recipient + event class and collapse the payload into the existing job.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Duplicate events within a window collapse
Unit test asserts two enqueues of the same recipient+class produce one job

unit_tests: Two enqueues with the same recipient_id + event_class collapse into a single job (the second is dropped/merged)
Events with a different event_class for the same recipient stay as separate jobs
Events with the same event_class but a different recipient_id stay separate
integration_tests: Events emitted from two different sources for the same recipient+class dedupe to one job
edge_cases: Concurrent enqueues do not produce two jobs (race)
testing_strategy.coverage_target: 100% of the dedupe path in queue.ex

security_considerations: The dedupe key must be scoped per recipient — collapsing across recipients would deliver one user's notification to another (cross-tenant leak)
The lookup for existing pending jobs must itself be scoped to the recipient_id
Collapse payloads without discarding the authorization context the dispatcher needs at send time
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use Oban unique-job support or a recipient-scoped pending-job lookup rather than an in-memory cache
Key strictly on {recipient_id, event_class}
pitfalls: Don't dedupe across recipients — a wrong key collapses one user's notification into another's
Don't rely on a non-atomic check-then-insert; use a DB-level uniqueness guard so a race can't produce two jobs
Don't collapse events of different classes into one job

goals.title: Build user notification preferences UI
goals.why: Users must explicitly opt in to channels (CAN-SPAM + GDPR); without preferences, nothing can be sent.
goals.what: Add a preferences LiveView, the user_notification_preferences schema, per-event-class opt-in toggles, per-user DND window, and email-address override.
goals.description: Independent of G1 and G3. Can be claimed in parallel with either.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
Preferences LiveView lets users opt in per event class
DND window persisted per user
Email-address override defaults to account email
Unsubscribe link in every notification routes back to this UI
pitfalls: Do not send any email to a user who has not explicitly opted in

tasks.title: Add user_notification_preferences schema and migration
tasks.description: Schema fields: user_id, channel (string), event_class (string), enabled (bool), dnd_start, dnd_end, email_override.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Schema + migration land
Default dnd window is 22:00-08:00 in the user's TZ

unit_tests: Changeset validates user_id, channel, event_class, enabled, dnd_start, dnd_end, email_override
Default DND window is 22:00-08:00 in the user's timezone
email_override must be a valid email format
integration_tests: mix ecto.migrate up then down runs cleanly and a preference row inserts
edge_cases: Duplicate (user_id, channel, event_class) rejected by the unique index

security_considerations: Every row is scoped to user_id with a FK to users; all reads/writes must filter by the current user — a preference row is per-tenant and must never be readable or writable by another user
email_override must be validated as an email and treated as unverified until confirmed, to prevent notification redirection
Add a unique index on (user_id, channel, event_class) to prevent conflicting duplicate rows
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Follow the existing Ecto schema + changeset conventions in lib/app/accounts/
Write a reversible migration with a FK to users and a unique index on (user_id, channel, event_class)
pitfalls: Don't store the email_override as trusted/verified — a raw override enables notification redirection
Don't omit the user_id foreign key and the unique index
Don't hardcode a UTC DND default — the window is expressed in the user's timezone

tasks.title: Add MyApp.Accounts.NotificationPreferences context
tasks.description: Context functions: get_preferences/1, update_preferences/2, channel_enabled?/3, dnd_active?/2. The dispatcher (G3) calls into this to decide whether to send.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
All four functions exist and have tests
channel_enabled? defaults to false for unrecognized channels

unit_tests: get_preferences/1 returns only the given user's preferences
update_preferences/2 persists changes and rejects a cross-user write
channel_enabled?/3 returns false for an unrecognized channel (fail closed)
dnd_active?/2 returns true inside a window that crosses midnight (22:00-08:00)
edge_cases: No preferences row -> safe default (treated as opted out)
dnd_active? exactly at the window boundary

security_considerations: All four functions take the current user/scope and must filter every query by user_id so one user can never read or update another's preferences
channel_enabled? must fail closed (return false) for unknown channels so an unexpected channel never sends without opt-in
update_preferences must reject writes targeting a different user_id (mass-assignment guard)
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Keep all Ecto queries in this context module, never in the LiveView (project rule)
Accept the current user/scope as the first argument and filter every query by user_id
pitfalls: Don't default channel_enabled? to true — unopted channels must be treated as disabled (CAN-SPAM/GDPR)
Don't let dnd_active? mishandle windows crossing midnight (22:00-08:00)
Don't expose a query that can return another user's preferences

tasks.title: Scaffold preferences LiveView mount and basic form
tasks.description: Mount loads the user's preferences via the context; render shows a per-event-class table with opt-in checkboxes.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Route /settings/notifications maps to the LiveView
Form renders one row per event class
Saving updates the database atomically

unit_tests: Route /settings/notifications mounts the LiveView and requires authentication
Mount loads only the current user's preferences
The form renders one row per event class
Saving persists all rows atomically
integration_tests: Toggle a channel, save, reload, and confirm the persisted state renders

security_considerations: The route must sit behind require_authenticated_user so only the owner edits their own preferences
Mount must load preferences for @current_scope.user only, never a user_id taken from params
Saving must not let a user set preferences for another user_id (mass-assignment guard on the changeset)
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Begin the template with <Layouts.app flash={@flash} current_scope={@current_scope}>
Place the route in the existing live_session :require_authenticated_user block; call the NotificationPreferences context — no Ecto in the LiveView
pitfalls: Don't read a user_id from params — always use @current_scope.user
Don't put Ecto queries in the LiveView; go through the context
Don't persist partial state non-atomically — write all rows in one transaction

tasks.title: Add DND time-window controls to preferences form
tasks.description: Add two time-picker inputs (start, end) for the user's DND window; persist on save.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Two time inputs render
Crossing midnight is supported (e.g., 22:00-08:00)
DND window persists across reloads

verification_steps.step_text: Set DND window 22:00-08:00 and confirm dnd_active? returns true at 23:00

unit_tests: Two time inputs (start, end) render and persist on save
A DND window crossing midnight (22:00-08:00) is stored correctly
manual_tests: Set the DND window to 22:00-08:00 and confirm dnd_active? returns true at 23:00

security_considerations: DND is a per-user setting — persist only to the current user's row
Reject a malformed time input server-side (don't trust the client widget) so it can't corrupt the dispatcher's send/skip decision
DND must never become a way to bypass the opt-in check — both are enforced independently at dispatch
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use the imported <.input type="time"> core component, not a hand-rolled widget
Persist through update_preferences/2 in the context
pitfalls: Don't assume start < end — the window can cross midnight
Don't validate the time only on the client; enforce it server-side
Don't let an empty DND window silently mean 'always DND' — treat it as no window

tasks.title: Add email-address override input + unsubscribe-link route
tasks.description: Email override input defaults to the account email; unsubscribe link uses a signed token route that opens the preferences page with the relevant channel toggle pre-focused.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Email override saves and is used by the dispatcher in G3
Unsubscribe route validates the signed token before showing the form

unit_tests: The email-override input defaults to the account email
The unsubscribe controller validates the signed token before rendering the form
An expired or tampered token is rejected
The token is scoped to a single {user, channel} pair
integration_tests: Following the unsubscribe link toggles off the correct channel and pre-focuses it in the UI
edge_cases: Token issued for a different user
testing_strategy.coverage_target: 100% of the unsubscribe controller and override save path

security_considerations: The unsubscribe token must be signed and unguessable and single-purpose (scoped to {user_id, channel}, not a general session grant) so it cannot be replayed to act as the user elsewhere
Validate the token before showing or mutating anything on the unsubscribe route

An email_override must be verified as owned by the user before the dispatcher uses it — an unverified override lets an attacker redirect a victim's notifications to their own inbox; consider token expiry
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Generate and verify the unsubscribe token with Phoenix.Token (or the app's existing signed-token helper), scoped to {user_id, channel}
Default the override input to @current_scope.user.email
pitfalls: Don't use a guessable or reusable token — scope it to user+channel and sign it
Don't send to an unverified email_override — verify ownership first to prevent notification redirection
Don't let the unsubscribe route perform any action before the token is validated

goals.title: Render notification emails and dispatch via Oban worker
goals.why: Once events land on the queue (G1) and users have opted in (G2), the dispatcher reads the queue and emits actual emails.
goals.what: Build the email-rendering pipeline (shared shell + per-event-class templates), wire the Oban worker that drains the :notifications queue, and add the per-message unsubscribe footer.
goals.description: Depends on G1 (the queue contract). Claim G1 first; this goal becomes claimable once G1's queue + dedupe land in main.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
Three event-class templates render (approval, mention, dependency-unblock)
Worker drains the queue and dispatches via the existing Mailer
Unsubscribe footer present in every email
Worker respects DND windows and channel opt-in from G2's preferences context
pitfalls: Do not bypass the existing audit-log infrastructure — every notification dispatch is logged
Do not send to a user whose preferences disable the channel

tasks.title: Define the email shell template (header, footer, unsubscribe link)
tasks.description: Shared HTML+text shell that wraps each event-class template. Includes the CAN-SPAM-compliant unsubscribe link with a signed token.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Shell renders for both HTML and plain-text variants
Unsubscribe link includes a signed user+channel token

unit_tests: The shell renders for both the HTML and plain-text variants
The unsubscribe link embeds a signed {user, channel} token
The CAN-SPAM footer is present in both variants
testing_strategy.coverage_target: 100% of the shell render entry point

security_considerations: The unsubscribe token embedded in every email must be signed and scoped to {user_id, channel} so it cannot be replayed for another user or purpose
Escape all interpolated user content in the HTML variant to prevent HTML/email injection
Don't embed secrets or internal IDs in the footer beyond the signed token
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Render both a text and an HTML variant like the existing mailer templates
Build the unsubscribe URL from the signed token via the router path helper
pitfalls: Don't ship an HTML-only shell — the plain-text variant is required
Don't build the unsubscribe link from a raw user_id — use a signed token
Don't omit the CAN-SPAM footer; it is non-negotiable

tasks.title: Render approval-owed email template
tasks.description: Per-event-class template for the approval flow. Plain text first; minimal HTML wrapper around it.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Template renders with the approval payload
Unit test asserts the rendered subject and body match the expected snapshot

unit_tests: The template renders with the approval payload and composes the shared shell
The rendered subject and body match the expected snapshot
User-supplied fields (requester name, task title) are HTML-escaped in the HTML variant

security_considerations: Render only fields the recipient is authorized to see — the approver may not have access to every attribute of the underlying record
Escape any user-supplied text (task title, requester name) in the HTML variant to prevent injection
Don't leak internal approval IDs or the identities of other approvers
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Render into the shared shell from the shell task, text-first then a minimal HTML variant
Follow the existing mailer template snapshot-test pattern
pitfalls: Don't render fields the approver isn't authorized to see
Don't skip HTML-escaping of the requester name / task title
Don't duplicate the shell header/footer — compose the shell

tasks.title: Render mention email template
tasks.description: Mention notification template; shows the comment excerpt + a deep link.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Template renders
Unit test covers escaping of user-supplied comment text

unit_tests: The template renders the comment excerpt and a deep link and composes the shell
A test explicitly covers escaping of user-supplied comment text (no HTML injection)
Long excerpts are truncated
edge_cases: Comment containing HTML or script markup
testing_strategy.coverage_target: 100% of the mention template incl. the escaping path

security_considerations: The comment excerpt is fully user-controlled — it MUST be HTML-escaped in the HTML variant to prevent injection / XSS-in-email
The deep link must not grant access on its own — the recipient still authenticates when they follow it
Truncate the excerpt so a malicious commenter cannot stuff the email with arbitrary content
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Escape the excerpt with the framework's HTML-escaping — never raw-interpolate it
Compose the shared shell and keep a plain-text variant
pitfalls: Don't raw-interpolate the comment excerpt — escape it (injection risk)
Don't include a deep link that bypasses authentication
Don't send the full comment body — excerpt and truncate it

tasks.title: Render dependency-unblocked email template
tasks.description: Per-event-class template for the dependency-unblock flow.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Template renders
Unit test asserts the rendered body names the unblocked task

unit_tests: The template renders and names the unblocked task
The body composes the shared shell and includes the plain-text variant

security_considerations: Name only the recipient's own unblocked task
Do not disclose details of the upstream blocking task the recipient may not have access to
Escape the task title in any HTML variant
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Compose the shared shell, text-first per the requirements
Follow the sibling template test pattern
pitfalls: Don't disclose the upstream blocking task's private details
Don't leave out the task name the recipient needs to act on
Don't skip the shell footer / unsubscribe link

tasks.title: Implement DispatchWorker that drains :notifications and respects preferences
tasks.description: Oban worker that pulls one job at a time, checks MyApp.Accounts.NotificationPreferences for channel_enabled? and dnd_active?, renders the appropriate template, and dispatches via the existing Mailer.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Worker honors channel opt-in (skips if disabled)
Worker honors DND window (delays the job if active)
Audit-log entry written for every dispatch
Unit tests cover the opt-out, DND-active, and happy-path branches

unit_tests: Opt-out branch: worker skips sending when channel_enabled? is false
DND-active branch: worker snoozes/reschedules the job past the window instead of sending
Happy path: worker renders the correct template, dispatches via the existing Mailer, and writes an audit-log entry
integration_tests: Enqueue an event, drain the queue, and confirm mail is sent only when the channel is enabled and outside the DND window
edge_cases: Preferences row missing -> fail closed (no send)

security_considerations: Re-check channel_enabled? and dnd_active? against the recipient's current preferences at send time — never trust a stale flag baked on the job — so a user who opted out is never emailed
Deliver only to the verified email/override for that exact recipient_id to prevent cross-tenant delivery
Write an audit-log entry for every dispatch but do NOT log the rendered notification body or payload (it contains user-visible content); fail closed if preferences can't be loaded
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Mirror the existing Oban worker pattern in lib/app/notifications/workers/ (use Oban.Worker, perform/1)
Dispatch through the existing Mailer and the existing audit-log infrastructure; gate on NotificationPreferences.channel_enabled?/dnd_active?
pitfalls: Don't send to a user whose preferences disable the channel — check at dispatch time
Don't bypass the audit-log infrastructure; every dispatch is logged
Don't log the rendered email body or payload — it contains user-visible content
Don't hard-delete a DND-blocked job — snooze/reschedule it past the window
